ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows triangle RST, point R is at the lower left, point T is at the lower right, and point S is above; there is a right-angle mark at S. Side RS is labeled 21, and side RT is labeled 44. Reasoning: Because the right angle is at S, RT is the hypotenuse, with length 44. What is required is angle T, and the side opposite angle T is RS, with length 21. Use the sine ratio: sin(T) = opposite side/hypotenuse = 21/44. Therefore T = arcsin(21/44) ≈ 28.4887°, rounded to nearest tenth gives 28.5°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as right triangle RST with the right-angle marker at S. From the labels, identify RS = 21 and RT = 44; since the right angle is at S, RT is the hypotenuse. The requested angle is at T, whose opposite side is RS. Use the sine ratio: sin(T) = opposite/hypotenuse = 21/44. Compute T = arcsin(21/44) and round to the nearest tenth, giving 28.5 degrees.
